narrationScript: Now it's your turn to build something practical: a simple Message Board with Flask! Your goal is to create a Flask application where users can submit messages and see all previously submitted messages on a single page. You'll set up your project with `app.py` and a `templates` folder containing `index.html`. Inside `app.py`, you'll maintain a simple Python list to simulate a database, storing each message as a dictionary. Your main route, `/`, will need to handle both GET and POST requests. For GET, it should render `index.html`, passing the list of messages. For POST, it will retrieve the message text and author from the submitted form, add it to your messages list, and crucially, redirect back to the `/` route to prevent accidental re-submissions. In `index.html`, you'll create a form for submitting new messages and then use a Jinja2 `for` loop to display all the messages from your list. This exercise will solidify your understanding of routes, request handling, form processing, and dynamic templating in Flask. Good luck!
